title: Error Handler route does not activate on module failure
problem: An Error Handler is attached to a module but does not activate when the module fails. The scenario stops with an error instead of routing to the error handler path.
symptoms: Scenario fails and stops at a module even though an Error Handler is attached
The Error Handler route does not appear to execute
Execution history shows failure at the module, not at a downstream Error Handler module

likely_causes.cause: The Error Handler is attached to the wrong module — it is attached to a downstream module instead of the one that is failing

diagnosis_steps: Identify the module producing the error and inspect its error-handler route and filters.
Check whether the error occurs before module execution and whether the chosen handler supports the intended behavior.

solutions.solution: Attach the Error Handler directly to the module that fails, not to a downstream module. Right-click the failing module and select 'Add error handler'.
solutions.conditions: When the Error Handler is attached to the wrong module

solutions.solution: Before using Rollback, inspect transaction support and the auto-commit setting; nontransactional actions cannot be undone.
solutions.conditions: Rollback is being considered after reviewing the actual failure.

prevention: Test the Error Handler explicitly by using 'Run once' with data that will trigger the error
Review Make's error types documentation to understand which directives apply to each error type

origin_details.source_name: Make Help Center — Rollback error handler
origin_details.evidence: Rollback depends on transaction support and auto-commit.

audit_notes: Removed unsupported claims about Ignore preventing route activation and universal rollback. Documentary review only; no verified real-case outcome.

evidence.claim: Rollback cannot reverse nontransactional module actions.

diagnostic_signals: Scenario fails and stops at a module even though an Error Handler is attached
The Error Handler route does not appear to execute
Execution history shows failure at the module, not at a downstream Error Handler module

title: Retry error handler (formerly Break) — stored failed bundle
problem: Retry stores the failed bundle for manual or configured automatic completion; other bundles can continue.
symptoms: Retry error handler (formerly Break) — stored failed bundle

likely_causes.cause: Retry stores the failed bundle for manual or configured automatic completion; other bundles can continue.

diagnosis_steps: Inspect the failed bundle, storage setting and automatic-completion configuration. Review previous writes before retrying.

solutions.solution: Enable incomplete-execution storage and select manual or automatic completion deliberately.
solutions.conditions: Only when retaining failed work is intended; correct persistent invalid data before reprocessing.

audit_notes: V1.4.1 editorial revision, documentation checked; no resolved real-world case. Previous inaccurate explanation replaced. Existing ID retained for compatibility.

evidence.claim: Retry stores the failed bundle for manual or configured automatic completion; other bundles can continue.
Break is the earlier name of Retry.

title: Resume directive — execution continues after error with a fallback value
problem: The Resume directive is configured on an Error Handler. When the module fails, Make continues execution from the next module using a fallback value defined in the Resume configuration. If the fallback value is incorrectly configured, downstream modules may receive unexpected data.
symptoms: Scenario continues after a module error but downstream data is incorrect or empty
The failing module's output is replaced by the Resume fallback value, which may be null or incorrectly typed
The execution completes successfully but the result is wrong

likely_causes.cause: The Resume fallback value is not configured or is empty — downstream modules receive null or undefined
The Resume fallback value type does not match what downstream modules expect

diagnosis_steps: Open the Error Handler attached to the failing module
Check the Resume directive configuration — verify the fallback value or bundle is correctly defined
Run the scenario with a case that triggers the error and inspect the bundle passed to downstream modules

solutions.solution: Configure the Resume fallback value to provide a structurally correct and typed output that downstream modules can process
solutions.conditions: When the Resume fallback is empty or typed incorrectly

solutions.solution: Add a Router after the resuming module to check for the fallback indicator and handle the error case differently from the success case
solutions.conditions: When the error path and success path require different downstream handling

prevention: Always configure a meaningful fallback value in the Resume directive
Test the Resume path explicitly with data that triggers the error

origin_details.source_name: Make Help Center — Error handling directives
origin_details.evidence: Resume directive is documented in Make Help Center.

audit_notes: Resume directive confirmed in Make documentation. Specific behavior of empty fallback value (producing null downstream) is inferred from Make's execution model — not explicitly stated in source.

evidence.claim: Resume directive is documented in Make Help Center.

The failing module's output is replaced by the Resume fallback value, which may be null or incorrectly typed
The execution completes successfully but the result is wrong

title: DataError — rejected data or incompatible function input
problem: DataError can indicate third-party validation rejection or an incompatible function argument.
symptoms: DataError — rejected data or incompatible function input

likely_causes.cause: DataError can indicate third-party validation rejection or an incompatible function argument.

diagnosis_steps: Compare the exact error with the mapped value and the function or receiving API contract. Distinguish BundleValidationError.

solutions.solution: Correct the value or conversion identified by that comparison.
solutions.conditions: Only after identifying the violated contract; a missing field alone does not establish DataError.

audit_notes: V1.4.1 editorial revision, documentation checked; no resolved real-world case. Previous inaccurate explanation replaced. Existing ID retained for compatibility.

evidence.claim: DataError can indicate third-party validation rejection or an incompatible function argument.

title: ConnectionError — unavailable external service
problem: ConnectionError can accompany an unavailable service and HTTP 503 or 504; it is not restricted to missing HTTP responses.

likely_causes.cause: ConnectionError can accompany an unavailable service and HTTP 503 or 504; it is not restricted to missing HTTP responses.

diagnosis_steps: Inspect the provider status, exact error and execution settings. Check whether earlier writes completed.

solutions.solution: Review delayed retry settings and incomplete-execution storage.
solutions.conditions: Only for a confirmed transient failure and when repeating the operation is safe.
